entries.name: sim_read
entries.declaration: long sim_read(long fd, void *buffer, long count)
entries.summary: Reads up to count bytes from the file descriptor in fd into the buffer at buffer, and returns how many it read. Descriptor 0 is standard input, so this is how a program reads what was typed. A return of 0 means end of input.

entries.name: sim_write
entries.declaration: long sim_write(long fd, const void *buffer, long count)
entries.summary: Writes count bytes from the buffer at buffer to the file descriptor in fd, and returns how many it wrote. Descriptor 1 is standard output and 2 is standard error, so this is how a program prints.

entries.name: sim_open
entries.declaration: long sim_open(const void *path, long flags, long mode)
entries.summary: Opens the path at path with the flags in flags and, when creating, the mode in mode. Returns a file descriptor.

entries.name: sim_close
entries.summary: Closes the file descriptor in fd.

entries.name: sim_stat
entries.summary: Reads file metadata for the path at path and writes it to the Linux struct stat buffer at statbuf.

entries.name: sim_fstat
entries.summary: Reads file metadata for the descriptor in fd and writes it to the Linux struct stat buffer at statbuf.

entries.name: sim_lstat
entries.summary: Like stat, but reports a symbolic link itself instead of the file it points to. Writes a Linux struct stat to the buffer at statbuf.

entries.name: sim_poll
entries.declaration: long sim_poll(void *fds, long nfds, long timeout)
entries.summary: Waits for the pollfd array at fds to report requested events, checking nfds entries for up to timeout milliseconds. A negative timeout waits without a time limit.

entries.name: sim_lseek
entries.declaration: long sim_lseek(long fd, long offset, long whence)
entries.summary: Moves the read and write position of the descriptor in fd to the offset in offset, interpreted according to whence, and returns the new position.

entries.name: sim_mmap
entries.declaration: long sim_mmap(void *address, long size, long prot, long flags, long fd, long offset)
entries.summary: Maps memory: the length in size, the protection in prot, the flags in flags. An anonymous private mapping is how a program asks for a block of memory it can write to. A MAP_PRIVATE mapping of a Project File copies its bytes into memory; writes to the mapping stay in memory. A MAP_SHARED mapping of a Project File returns -ENODEV.

entries.name: sim_mprotect
entries.declaration: long sim_mprotect(void *address, long size, long prot)
entries.summary: Changes the read, write, or execute permissions of the size bytes starting at the page-aligned address in address.

entries.name: sim_munmap
entries.summary: Unmaps the mapping of size bytes at the address in address.

entries.name: sim_brk
entries.summary: Sets the end address of the heap area. Returns the current break; a request the emulator cannot satisfy leaves it unchanged.

entries.name: sim_rt_sigaction
entries.declaration: long sim_rt_sigaction(long sig, const void *act, void *oldact, long count)

entries.name: sim_rt_sigprocmask
entries.declaration: long sim_rt_sigprocmask(long how, const void *set, void *oldset, long count)

entries.name: sim_ioctl
entries.declaration: long sim_ioctl(long fd, long request, void *arg)
entries.summary: Asks a device the descriptor in fd refers to for something outside the ordinary read and write interface, chosen by the request in request.

entries.name: sim_pread64
entries.declaration: long sim_pread64(long fd, void *buffer, long count, long offset)

entries.name: sim_pwrite64
entries.declaration: long sim_pwrite64(long fd, const void *buffer, long count, long offset)

entries.name: sim_readv
entries.declaration: long sim_readv(long fd, const void *iov, long count)
entries.summary: Reads into the buffers listed by the iovec array at iov, with count entries, from the descriptor in fd; returns the total bytes read. An error in a later buffer can be returned after earlier buffers have already changed, rather than returning the earlier partial byte count. Check those buffers before retrying after an error.

entries.name: sim_writev
entries.declaration: long sim_writev(long fd, const void *iov, long count)
entries.summary: Writes the buffers listed by the iovec array at iov, with count entries, to the descriptor in fd; returns the total bytes written. The buffers are gathered into one payload before writing. If a capacity limit refuses the write, none of that payload is written.

entries.name: sim_pipe
entries.summary: Creates a pair of connected file descriptors and writes both integers to the two-element array at pfds; reads from one end receive bytes written to the other.

entries.name: sim_select
entries.declaration: long sim_select(long number, void *fds1, void *fds2, void *fds3, void *timeout)
entries.summary: Takes the descriptor limit in number, pointers to the read, write, and exception sets in fds1, fds2, and fds3, and an optional timeout in timeout. Waits until a descriptor is ready or the timeout expires, then updates the sets and timeout.

entries.name: sim_mremap
entries.declaration: long sim_mremap(void *oldaddress, long oldsize, long newsize, long flags, void *newaddress)

entries.name: sim_msync
entries.declaration: long sim_msync(void *address, long size, long flags)

entries.name: sim_madvise
entries.declaration: long sim_madvise(void *address, long size, long advice)

entries.name: sim_dup
entries.summary: Returns a new file descriptor that refers to the same open file description as the descriptor in fd.

entries.name: sim_dup2
entries.summary: Makes descriptor number refer to the same open file description as fd, closing the old number first if needed.

entries.name: sim_nanosleep
entries.summary: Sleeps for the interval at request, a pair of seconds and nanoseconds.

entries.name: sim_getitimer
entries.summary: Writes the remaining delay and repeat interval of the timer selected by which to the itimerval structure at current. Only ITIMER_REAL is supported. ITIMER_VIRTUAL and ITIMER_PROF return -EOPNOTSUPP.

entries.name: sim_setitimer
entries.declaration: long sim_setitimer(long which, const void *value, void *oldvalue)
entries.summary: Sets the timer selected by which from the itimerval structure at value, and writes the previous settings at oldvalue when that pointer is nonzero. Only ITIMER_REAL is supported; it sends SIGALRM when its delay expires. ITIMER_VIRTUAL and ITIMER_PROF return -EOPNOTSUPP.

entries.name: sim_sendfile
entries.declaration: long sim_sendfile(long outfd, long infd, void *offset, long count)
entries.summary: Copies up to count bytes from the input descriptor in infd to the output descriptor in outfd, optionally updating the input position through the pointer in offset.

entries.name: sim_exit
entries.summary: Ends the program with the status in status. It never returns, and a program that reaches the end of its code without calling it runs into whatever bytes follow.

entries.name: sim_wait4
entries.declaration: long sim_wait4(long pid, void *wstatus, long options, void *rusage)
entries.summary: Returns -ECHILD immediately because this environment has no child processes.

entries.name: sim_uname
entries.summary: Writes system name and version fields to the Linux struct utsname buffer at buffer.

entries.name: sim_fcntl
entries.declaration: long sim_fcntl(long fd, long cmd, long arg)

entries.name: sim_getcwd
entries.summary: Writes the current working directory as a NUL-terminated path to the buffer at buffer, up to count bytes.

entries.name: sim_chdir
entries.summary: Changes the program’s current working directory to the path at path.

entries.name: sim_fchdir
entries.summary: Changes the program’s current working directory to the directory referred to by descriptor fd.

entries.name: sim_rename
entries.summary: Renames or moves the path at path1 to the path at path2. Within /project, moving a directory returns -EISDIR and replacing an existing destination File returns -EEXIST.

entries.name: sim_mkdir
entries.summary: Makes a directory at the path in path, with the mode in mode. Under /project it lasts for the run, and Files can be created in it: the first one keeps it in the Project, since Project directories exist only as prefixes of File paths. One still empty when the program ends is gone.

entries.name: sim_rmdir
entries.summary: Removes the empty directory named by the path at path. Under /project, a directory that holds Files returns -ENOTEMPTY, and one that does not disappears by itself when its last File is removed; an empty one made by mkdir is removed.

entries.name: sim_unlink
entries.summary: Removes the directory entry named by the path at path; an open file remains available through its descriptor. Under /project, removing a directory’s last File also removes that implicit directory.

entries.name: sim_readlink
entries.declaration: long sim_readlink(const void *path, void *buffer, long count)

entries.name: sim_chown
entries.declaration: long sim_chown(const void *path, long uid, long gid)

entries.name: sim_fchown
entries.declaration: long sim_fchown(long fd, long uid, long gid)

entries.name: sim_lchown
entries.declaration: long sim_lchown(const void *path, long uid, long gid)

entries.name: sim_gettimeofday
entries.summary: Writes calendar time since the Unix epoch, in seconds and microseconds, to the timeval structure at timeval. Interactive runs use host calendar time; Testcases use 2000-01-01 UTC plus virtual elapsed time.

entries.name: sim_getrusage
entries.summary: Writes resource-usage counters for the selected process or children to the rusage structure at usage.

entries.name: sim_sysinfo
entries.summary: Writes the emulator’s uptime, memory, and process-count values to a Linux struct sysinfo buffer at info.

entries.name: sim_ptrace
entries.declaration: long sim_ptrace(long value1, long value2, long value3, long value4)

entries.name: sim_getgroups
entries.summary: Writes up to size supplementary group IDs to the array at groups; with a zero size, returns how many IDs are needed.

entries.name: sim_setgroups
entries.summary: Replaces the process’s supplementary group list with the size group IDs in the array at groups.

entries.name: sim_setresuid
entries.declaration: long sim_setresuid(long uid1, long uid2, long uid3)

entries.name: sim_setresgid
entries.declaration: long sim_setresgid(long gid1, long gid2, long gid3)

entries.name: sim_prctl
entries.declaration: long sim_prctl(long value1, long value2, long value3, long value4, long value5)

entries.name: sim_time
entries.summary: Returns calendar time in whole seconds since the Unix epoch, and also stores it at the address in buffer unless buffer is 0. Interactive runs use host calendar time; Testcases use 2000-01-01 UTC plus virtual elapsed time.

entries.name: sim_futex
entries.declaration: long sim_futex(long value1, long value2, long value3, long value4, long value5, long value6)

entries.name: sim_sched_getaffinity
entries.declaration: long sim_sched_getaffinity(long pid, long size, void *mask)

entries.name: sim_getdents64
entries.declaration: long sim_getdents64(long fd, void *dirents, long count)

entries.name: sim_fadvise64
entries.declaration: long sim_fadvise64(long value1, long value2, long value3, long value4)

entries.name: sim_clock_gettime
entries.summary: Writes the clock selected by clockid to the timespec structure at tp (seconds and nanoseconds). CLOCK_REALTIME, CLOCK_REALTIME_COARSE and CLOCK_TAI report Unix epoch time: host calendar time interactively, and 2000-01-01 UTC plus virtual elapsed time in Testcases. CLOCK_TAI shares realtime without a leap-second offset. CLOCK_PROCESS_CPUTIME_ID and CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID count executed instructions at nominal 100 MHz, exclude waiting time, and rewind with Undo. Monotonic clocks and CLOCK_BOOTTIME report elapsed time; virtual elapsed time advances only through waits.

entries.name: sim_clock_nanosleep
entries.declaration: long sim_clock_nanosleep(long clockid, long number, const void *request, void *remaining)

entries.name: sim_exit_group
entries.summary: Ends every thread of the program with the status in status. For a program with one thread it is exit.

entries.name: sim_tgkill
entries.declaration: long sim_tgkill(long value1, long value2, long value3)

entries.name: sim_openat
entries.declaration: long sim_openat(long dirfd, const void *string, long flags, long mode)

entries.name: sim_mkdirat
entries.declaration: long sim_mkdirat(long dirfd, const void *path, long mode)
entries.summary: Makes a directory at the path in path, relative to the directory descriptor in dirfd, with the mode in mode. Under /project it lasts for the run, and Files can be created in it: the first one keeps it in the Project, since Project directories exist only as prefixes of File paths. One still empty when the program ends is gone.

entries.name: sim_fchownat
entries.declaration: long sim_fchownat(long dirfd, const void *path, long uid, long gid, long flags)

entries.name: sim_futimesat
entries.declaration: long sim_futimesat(long dirfd, const void *path, const void *times)

entries.name: sim_newfstatat
entries.declaration: long sim_newfstatat(long dirfd, const void *path, void *statbuf, long flags)

entries.name: sim_unlinkat
entries.declaration: long sim_unlinkat(long dirfd, const void *path, long flags)

entries.name: sim_renameat
entries.declaration: long sim_renameat(long dirfd1, const void *path1, long dirfd2, const void *path2)
entries.summary: Renames or moves the path at path1, relative to the directory descriptor in dirfd1, to the path at path2, relative to the directory descriptor in dirfd2. Within /project, moving a directory returns -EISDIR and replacing an existing destination File returns -EEXIST.

entries.name: sim_linkat
entries.declaration: long sim_linkat(long dirfd1, const void *path1, long dirfd2, const void *path2, long flags)

entries.name: sim_symlinkat
entries.declaration: long sim_symlinkat(const void *path1, long dirfd, const void *path2)

entries.name: sim_readlinkat
entries.declaration: long sim_readlinkat(long dirfd, const void *string, void *buffer, long count)

entries.name: sim_fchmodat
entries.declaration: long sim_fchmodat(long dirfd, const void *path, long mode)

entries.name: sim_faccessat
entries.declaration: long sim_faccessat(long dirfd, const void *path, long mode)

entries.name: sim_pselect6
entries.declaration: long sim_pselect6(long nfds, void *readfds, void *writefds, void *exceptfds, const void *timeout, const void *sigmask)

entries.name: sim_ppoll
entries.declaration: long sim_ppoll(void *fds, long nfds, const void *timeout, const void *sigmask, long sigsetsize)

entries.name: sim_get_robust_list
entries.declaration: long sim_get_robust_list(long value1, long value2, long value3)

entries.name: sim_utimensat
entries.declaration: long sim_utimensat(long dirfd, const void *path, const void *times, long flags)

entries.name: sim_dup3
entries.declaration: long sim_dup3(long fd, long number, long flags)

entries.name: sim_preadv
entries.declaration: long sim_preadv(long fd, const void *iov, long count, long offset)

entries.name: sim_pwritev
entries.declaration: long sim_pwritev(long fd, const void *iov, long count, long offset)
entries.summary: Writes the buffers listed by the iovec array at iov, with count entries, to the descriptor in fd at the offset in offset; returns the total bytes written without changing the descriptor’s position. The buffers are gathered into one payload before writing. If a capacity limit refuses the write, none of that payload is written.

entries.name: sim_prlimit64
entries.declaration: long sim_prlimit64(long pid, long resource, const void *rlim1, void *rlim2)

entries.name: sim_renameat2
entries.declaration: long sim_renameat2(long dirfd1, const void *path1, long dirfd2, const void *path2, long flags)
entries.summary: Renames or moves paths relative to the directory descriptors in dirfd1 and dirfd2, using the flags in flags. RENAME_NOREPLACE refuses an existing destination; RENAME_EXCHANGE swaps two existing names. Within /project, directory moves return -EISDIR and an ordinary rename that would replace an existing File returns -EEXIST.

entries.name: sim_getrandom
entries.declaration: long sim_getrandom(void *buffer, long count, long number)

entries.name: sim_preadv2
entries.declaration: long sim_preadv2(long fd, const void *iov, long count, long offset, long value, long number)

entries.name: sim_pwritev2
entries.declaration: long sim_pwritev2(long fd, const void *iov, long count, long offset, long value, long number)

entries.name: sim_rseq
entries.declaration: long sim_rseq(long value1, long value2, long value3, long value4)

entries.name: sim_close_range
entries.declaration: long sim_close_range(long value1, long value2, long value3)

entries.name: sim_faccessat2
entries.declaration: long sim_faccessat2(long dirfd, const void *path, long mode, long flags)

entries.name: gettimeofday
entries.summary: Stores the current time, CLOCK_REALTIME, in *tv, in seconds and microseconds since 1970-01-01 UTC. Pass NULL for tz. Returns 0, or -1 with errno set.

entries.name: setitimer
entries.declaration: int setitimer(int which, const struct itimerval *value, struct itimerval *old)
entries.summary: Sets the interval timer which from *value, and stores its previous setting in *old unless old is NULL. ITIMER_REAL sends SIGALRM each time it expires, which ends the program unless signal or sigaction from <signal.h> gave it a handler first. Returns 0, or -1 with errno set: EOPNOTSUPP for ITIMER_VIRTUAL and ITIMER_PROF.

entries.name: getitimer
entries.summary: Stores in *value the time until the interval timer which expires, and its interval. Returns 0, or -1 with errno set.

entries.name: select
entries.declaration: int select(int nfds, fd_set *readfds, fd_set *writefds, fd_set *exceptfds, struct timeval *timeout)
entries.summary: Waits for readiness: readfds for reading, writefds for writing, and exceptfds for exceptional conditions (POLLPRI). Set nfds to one more than the highest descriptor in any set. Pass NULL for an unused set or an unlimited timeout; a zero timeout only checks. On success, the sets contain only ready descriptors. Returns the total number of ready bits across all sets, 0 on timeout, or -1 with errno set. One descriptor can count in more than one set. The sets and *timeout are modified; prepare them again before another wait. *timeout holds the remaining time.

entries.name: clock_gettime
entries.summary: Reads the time from clockid into *tp as seconds and nanoseconds. Returns 0, or -1 with errno set (EINVAL for an unknown clock).

entries.name: nanosleep
entries.declaration: int nanosleep(const struct timespec *request, struct timespec *remaining)
entries.summary: Waits for the duration in *request. Returns 0 on completion, or -1 with errno set. If a signal interrupts the wait, errno is EINTR and *remaining receives the time left, unless remaining is NULL.

entries.name: rename
entries.summary: Renames or moves the file at from to the path to. Returns 0, or -1 with errno set. Under /project a file at to stays and the call fails with EEXIST, and a folder cannot move (EISDIR).

entries.name: remove
entries.summary: Deletes the file at path, or the folder at path when it is empty, as unlink and rmdir do. Returns 0, or -1 with errno set.

entries.name: read
entries.declaration: ssize_t read(int fd, void *buffer, size_t count)
entries.summary: Reads up to count bytes from fd into buffer. Returns the byte count, which may be less than count, 0 at end of input, or -1 with errno set. EAGAIN means a nonblocking descriptor has no input ready. For an input device, a buffer smaller than one input_event fails with EINVAL.

entries.name: write
entries.declaration: ssize_t write(int fd, const void *buffer, size_t count)
entries.summary: Writes up to count bytes from buffer to fd. Returns the byte count, or -1 with errno set. After a short successful write, submit the remaining bytes in another call. EAGAIN means a nonblocking descriptor cannot accept any bytes now.

entries.name: close
entries.summary: Closes fd. Returns 0, or -1 with errno set.

entries.name: getpid
entries.summary: Returns the program's process ID, which can be passed to kill. This call does not fail.

entries.name: lseek
entries.declaration: off_t lseek(int fd, off_t offset, int whence)
entries.summary: Sets the byte position of fd to offset relative to the start (SEEK_SET), current position (SEEK_CUR) or end (SEEK_END). Returns the new position, or -1 with errno set. The Terminal and devices other than /dev/fb0 have no seek position and fail with ESPIPE.

entries.name: isatty
entries.summary: Returns 1 if fd refers to the Terminal or console. Otherwise returns 0 with errno set: ENOTTY for a file or another device, EBADF for a descriptor that is not open.

entries.name: fsync
entries.summary: Synchronizes pending file changes for fd. On /dev/fb0, requests an immediate update of the Screen from the framebuffer. Returns 0, or -1 with errno set.

entries.name: unlink
entries.summary: Deletes the file at path. A descriptor already open on it keeps reading and writing it. Returns 0, or -1 with errno set: ENOENT if there is no such file, EISDIR for a folder, which rmdir deletes.

entries.name: rmdir
entries.summary: Deletes the empty folder at path. Returns 0, or -1 with errno set: ENOTEMPTY while it holds anything, ENOENT if there is no such folder.

entries.name: usleep
entries.summary: Waits for the requested number of microseconds. Returns 0 on completion, or -1 with errno set; EINTR means a signal interrupted the wait.

entries.name: sleep
entries.summary: Waits for the requested number of seconds. Returns 0 on completion, or the whole seconds remaining if a signal interrupts the wait.

entries.name: open
entries.summary: Opens the file or device at path, such as "/dev/fb0", using flags such as O_RDWR or O_RDONLY | O_NONBLOCK. With O_CREAT, supply a third argument for the new file mode, such as 0644. Returns a file descriptor, or -1 with errno set. ENOENT means the path does not exist; ENODEV means the device is unavailable here.

entries.name: fcntl
entries.summary: Applies cmd to fd. Commands that need a value take a third argument. For example, fcntl(fd, F_SETFL, fcntl(fd, F_GETFL) | O_NONBLOCK) enables nonblocking I/O. Returns the command's result, or -1 with errno set.

entries.name: ioctl
entries.declaration: int ioctl(int fd, unsigned long request, ...)
entries.summary: Applies request to the device open on fd. The request defines whether the third argument is a pointer, an immediate integer or unused; check its device reference. Returns the request's result, usually 0, or -1 with errno set. ENOTTY means the device does not support the request; EINVAL means an invalid argument.

entries.name: mmap
entries.declaration: void *mmap(void *address, size_t length, int prot, int flags, int fd, off_t offset)
entries.summary: Maps length bytes of fd starting at offset into the program's address space. If address is NULL, the system chooses the address. For the Screen, use mmap(NULL, fix.smem_len, PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE, MAP_SHARED, fd, 0). Returns the mapped address, or MAP_FAILED with errno set.

entries.name: munmap
entries.summary: Removes the mapping of length bytes at address. Returns 0, or -1 with errno set.

entries.name: poll
entries.declaration: int poll(struct pollfd *fds, nfds_t nfds, int timeout)
entries.summary: Checks the first nfds elements of fds. Each events field requests readiness, such as POLLIN for reading or POLLOUT for writing; revents receives the resulting flags. Waits up to timeout milliseconds (-1 waits indefinitely, 0 only checks). Returns the number of array elements with nonzero revents, 0 on timeout, or -1 with errno set.

entries.name: tcgetattr
entries.summary: Reads the terminal settings for fd into *termios. Returns 0, or -1 with errno set (ENOTTY if fd is not a terminal). The c_cc array contains 19 control-character slots used by the kernel; later slots are zero. c_ispeed and c_ospeed reflect the baud-rate bits in c_cflag.

entries.name: tcsetattr
entries.declaration: int tcsetattr(int fd, int action, const struct termios *termios)
entries.summary: Applies *termios to terminal fd. action selects when: TCSANOW applies immediately, TCSADRAIN waits for output to drain, and TCSAFLUSH also discards unread input after draining output. These use TCSETS, TCSETSW and TCSETSF respectively. Returns 0, or -1 with errno set.

entries.name: tcflush
entries.summary: Discards queued terminal data on fd: unread input for TCIFLUSH, unsent output for TCOFLUSH, or both for TCIOFLUSH. Returns 0, or -1 with errno set.

entries.name: tcdrain
entries.summary: Waits until all output written to terminal fd has been sent. The editor's Terminal drains immediately. Returns 0, or -1 with errno set.

entries.name: cfmakeraw
entries.summary: Disables line buffering, echo, signal-generating control characters, input translations and output processing in *termios. Apply the changed settings with tcsetattr. Input remains a byte stream; special keys can produce escape sequences. Output '\n' no longer supplies '\r', so write '\r\n' for a new line.

entries.name: stat
entries.summary: Describes the file at path in *buffer, following a symbolic link to what it names. Returns 0, or -1 with errno set (ENOENT when there is no such file).

entries.name: fstat
entries.summary: Describes the file or device open on fd in *buffer. Returns 0, or -1 with errno set.

entries.name: lstat
entries.summary: As stat, but describes a symbolic link itself rather than what it names. Returns 0, or -1 with errno set.

entries.name: mkdir
entries.summary: Makes the folder path, with the permission bits in mode, such as 0755. Its parent must exist. Returns 0, or -1 with errno set: EEXIST if something has the name already, ENOENT if the parent does not exist. Under /project a new folder lasts for the run, and the first file made in it keeps it in the Project.

entries.name: opendir
entries.summary: Opens a directory stream for path, such as "/dev/input", for use with readdir. Returns a DIR pointer, or NULL with errno set (ENOENT if the path does not exist, ENOTDIR if it is not a directory).

entries.name: readdir
entries.summary: Returns the next entry in dir, including "." and "..", in no guaranteed order. Returns NULL at end of directory without changing errno, or on error with errno set. To distinguish the two, set errno to 0 before the call and inspect it after a NULL result. The returned entry is valid until the next readdir or closedir on this stream.

entries.name: rewinddir
entries.summary: Resets dir to the beginning so the next readdir returns its first entry again.

entries.name: dirfd
entries.summary: Returns the file descriptor used by dir, for calls such as fstat or openat. closedir closes that descriptor.

entries.name: closedir
entries.summary: Closes the directory stream and frees its memory. The DIR pointer and entries returned by readdir are no longer valid. Returns 0, or -1 with errno set.

entries.name: sigfillset
entries.summary: Fills *set with every signal except 32 and 33, which are reserved by the C library. Returns 0.

entries.name: sigaddset
entries.summary: Adds sig to *set. Returns 0, or -1 with errno set to EINVAL for an invalid signal number.

entries.name: sigdelset
entries.summary: Removes sig from *set. Returns 0, or -1 with errno set to EINVAL for an invalid signal number.

entries.name: sigismember
entries.summary: Returns 1 if sig belongs to *set, or 0 otherwise. Returns -1 with errno set to EINVAL for an invalid signal number.

entries.name: sigprocmask
entries.declaration: int sigprocmask(int how, const sigset_t *set, sigset_t *old)
entries.summary: Changes the blocked signal set: SIG_BLOCK adds *set, SIG_UNBLOCK removes *set, and SIG_SETMASK replaces the blocked set with *set. A NULL set leaves it unchanged. If old is not NULL, stores the previous blocked set in *old. A blocked signal remains pending until unblocked. Returns 0, or -1 with errno set.

entries.name: sigaction
entries.declaration: int sigaction(int sig, const struct sigaction *action, struct sigaction *old)
entries.summary: Installs *action for sig; a NULL action leaves it unchanged. If old is not NULL, stores the previous action in *old. For example: struct sigaction action = { 0 }; action.sa_handler = handler; sigaction(SIGINT, &action, NULL). Returns 0, or -1 with errno set. SIGKILL and SIGSTOP cannot have their actions changed (EINVAL).

entries.name: signal
entries.summary: Installs handler for sig. Pass a function taking the signal number, SIG_DFL to restore the default action, or SIG_IGN to ignore the signal. For example: signal(SIGINT, on_ctrl_c). Uses SA_RESTART so eligible interrupted calls restart automatically; see the syscall reference for restart rules. Returns the previous handler or action, or SIG_ERR with errno set.

entries.name: kill
entries.summary: Sends sig to process pid. Use getpid() from <unistd.h> to identify this program. Returns 0, or -1 with errno set (ESRCH if no such process exists).

entries.name: raise
entries.summary: Sends sig to this program. An unblocked signal with a handler runs that handler before raise returns. A blocked signal remains pending until unblocked. SIG_IGN discards the signal; SIG_DFL applies its default action, which may end the program. Returns 0, or -1 with errno set.
